candidate.mistake_reason: At step 29, the Orchestrator prematurely declared the request satisfied and moved to finalize an answer without actually identifying the word deleted in the last amendment to Rule 601. Despite instructing WebSurfer to check the last amendment details, it did not ensure those details were retrieved from the page (e.g., scrolling to Notes/advisory committee amendments) and instead proceeded, which led to the later incorrect guess.
candidate.first_mistake: This is the first step where the workflow deviated toward the wrong outcome. Up to step 28, navigation was correct (to Article VI and Rule 601). candidate.mistake_not_corrected: No later agent corrected this. The session then terminated without correction.

This misjudgment directly led to finalizing with an incorrect guess and was not corrected later. While one could argue WebSurfer had not completed the requested check, the decisive first mistake causing the wrong outcome is the Orchestrator’s premature closure at step 29.

There is no earlier evident mistake that relates to the final wrong outcome, so Step 29 is plausibly the first misstep causing the error.
